subject: [IaC review] VPC peering + CNI ops: gaps and CI gating
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VPC peering + CNI changes for ACME private stack - request for IaC review

Folks —

Circling back on the ACME private deployment work: we completed a draft that wires up a pair of service VPCs (app + infra) with a dedicated peering link and deploys Calico CNI with eBPF offload for perf. Key artifacts attached: peering diagram and the helm-values we plan to apply in the private cluster.

Asks:
- Can you review the Terraform peering module and the routing table split? There are two main subnets: svc-subnet (internal only) and mgmt-subnet (bastion, CI runners).
- Validate the CNI iam/service-account assumptions (node-role vs daemonset SA) — we changed the SA scope to allow ENI attachment to the host.
- CI gating: propose a presubmit that runs the privdeploy-integ-e2e job against a staging emulation environment before merging.

Notes / potential risk areas:
- NAT throughput: we plan to keep egress via a shared NAT GW in the infra VPC; this may be a capacity hot spot for high-throughput inference imports.
- Peering routes: the terraform currently writes full-route propagation for the infra VPC which could accidentally expose management subnets; want to ensure RBAC and routing controls are explicit.

Attachments: 2026-11-25_peering-diagram.pdf (diagram), helm-values-site.yaml (helm values snippet)

Thanks,
Karthik
---
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Matt Li <matt@acme.io>, ACME Security <security@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC peering + CNI changes for ACME private stack - request for IaC review

Karthik — thanks for the draft. I skimmed the artifacts and left a few inline questions below. Quoting your notes for context.

On Wed, 25 Nov 2026 at 09:12, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Circling back on the ACME private deployment work: we completed a draft that wires up a pair of service VPCs (app + infra) with a dedicated peering link and deploys Calico CNI with eBPF offload for perf.

Comments / requested changes:
- Routing: Do not enable automatic route propagation for the infra VPC. Instead, the terraform should explicitly create the peering routes per-subnet. I'll add a small helper module to generate route blocks from a JSON map so we avoid accidental 0.0.0.0/0 exposures.
- NAT throughput: add a quota check in the terraform plan step that fails the plan if projected bytes/sec for the NAT GW exceeds the account baseline. We need to capture expected token ingestion rates from the product team (requesting numbers from Marissa).
- CNI SA: the current helm-values give the daemonset broad ec2:AttachNetworkInterface permissions. Change to a narrow policy that uses a short-lived token process for attaching interfaces — we'll prototype a small sidecar to call STS instead of giving the daemonset static rights.
- CI gating: presubmit should include a smoke e2e that validates: health probes, peered route visibility, and a synthetic small-batch inference to verify KV cache is not leaking across VPCs. Add a flake-tolerant retry for the e2e run (3 attempts).

Action items (initial):
- @marissa_cole: collect ACME token ingestion numbers and confirm expected egress profile.
- @hannah_schmitt: add the route-generator helper and run a cross-account plan in a sandbox.
- @karthik_iyer: narrow the SA policy and attach a design note about sidecar STS flow.

Matt / ACME security — tagging you on the plan. Two quick questions for you: 1) do you have a mandatory list of controls we must show in the evidence pack for peering (e.g., routing-table change logs, cross-account flow logs), and 2) are signed helm charts required for your procurement?

Irene
Irene Choi
Dir, Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
From: Matt Li <matt@acme.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC peering + CNI changes for ACME private stack - request for IaC review

Irene / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of asks from ACME security side: 
1) Evidence: we need both routing-table change logs and VPC flow logs covering the peering interfaces for the last 90 days before go-live. The routing audit should include who initiated the change (IAM principal) and the terraform plan output tied to the PR.
2) Signed charts: yes — for our procurement we require provenance for charts. If you can provide a signed-chart .tgz (cosigned) for the calico chart we can accept that.

One more technical ask: any chance to avoid NAT for some high-throughput ingestion (we prefer a direct private link for large blob imports). If you can propose a short-term alternate path (S3 VPC endpoint in the infra VPC with prefix lists + transfer acceleration), that would help us mitigate NAT spikes.

We appreciate the sidecar idea for STS — that aligns with our least-priv model.

Matt
Matt Li
Security Engineering, ACME Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: VPC peering + CNI changes for ACME private stack - request for IaC review

Quick summary and next steps — team please treat as authoritative for the sprint card.

Summary of agreed changes:
- Routing: explicit peering route blocks only; no auto-propagation. Hannah to land route-generator helper.
- CNI: narrow the daemonset permissions; Karthik to prototype STS sidecar and update helm-values accordingly. Signed calico chart requested by ACME; security to coordinate chart-signing process with release engineering.
- NAT: Marissa to provide ingestion numbers and approve adding an S3 VPC endpoint plan as a mitigation path. We will include a short-term bypass path for blobs.
- CI gating: add privdeploy-integ-e2e presubmit with three retry attempts, smoke checks, and a link to JIRA PRIVDEPLOY-478 for tracking.

Deliverables / owners / ETA:
- Marissa Cole: supply ingestion profile (due 2026-11-29)
- Hannah Schmitt: route-generator PR (due 2026-12-02)
- Karthik Iyer: STS sidecar prototype + helm-values PR (due 2026-12-07)
- Irene Choi: evidence checklist and required log formats for ACME (due 2026-12-03)

Attachments: 2026-11-26_action-items.md (action list + PR links)

I'll open the JIRA and create the presubmit job template after Hannah's PR lands. If there are blockers on chart signing, loop in release-eng and I'll escalate to the procurement SLA.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
